correctness.rationale: For each of \(n\in\{6,7,8\}\), the exact program constructs all valid matchings and confirms a second independent face enumeration. It checks all directed Hasse covering edges for acyclicity (3,990; 15,036; 55,256). The resulting geometric matching has one critical 0-cell and precisely the specified high-dimensional cells. Signed gradient-path substitution gives full integral Morse differentials; all consecutive compositions vanish. Elementary integer ±1-pivot row/column reductions give ranks (\(n=6\): 2 and 3; \(n=7\): 8; \(n=8\): 2 and 19) with zero residual. All lowest positive cells are thereby cancelled. Remaining adjacent attaching maps are classified by their integer degree matrices, so the primitive pivots yield exactly wedges 10 \(S^3\); 16 \(S^4\); and 2 \(S^4\) plus 4 \(S^5\), integrally. Independently, mod-2 ranks from complete original simplicial boundary matrices corroborate the result. Finite computations are exhaustive only for three orders; no unjustified infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 arXiv full text explicitly names the ordinary matching complexes of Möbius ladders as a future problem (Problem 26), having treated independence and perfect matching complexes instead. published-finding corpus searches for identical parameters and altered names recovered smaller \(M_{8}\) and \(M_{10}\) ordinary matching cases, other graph families, and Möbius total-cut/perfect-matching results, but no \(n\in\{6,7,8\}\) ordinary statement. The 2019 open small-grid, 2023 open polygonal-string and 2024 outerplanar scopes do not cover the closed nonplanar Möbius ladder. Exact computations and source comparison support best-knowledge originality; unindexed overlap and incomplete records remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed, unpublished or inaccessible mathematical work could already give one or more exact \(M_{12}\)/\(M_{14}\)/\(M_{16}\) homotopy types.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper explicitly identifies ordinary matching complexes as an open graph-family problem. Three consecutive natural orders are settled integrally beyond previously indexed small cases, including a mixed-dimensional \(M_{16}\) homotopy type that cannot be deduced from the perfect matching complex or a single Betti number. Exact finite homotopy information restricts future recurrence or periodicity conjectures. The choice is natural (the next three unclassified graph orders), not an arbitrary slice or incremental parameter tweak; the package states its finite scope and avoids extrapolation.
